::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Aug 26th [1868]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS University of Iowa; MsL/Y56
:::

Dear [Miss Finchcliffe](people/person_511.qmd),
I am very glad to have seen [Edith Crawley’](people/person_382.qmd)s letter which I return with many thanks.[^1] I had proposed the Irishwoman to [Mrs Gray](people/person_579.qmd) for the Cape ladies, and she had rejected her, but perhaps they know their own plans best. I am glad that another and elder lady has been added to them for someone to take the command was much wanted.

I am glad that dear [Miss Mackenzie](people/person_930.qmd) is so much better, but it has been a long illness. These last two or three days have been very sad with us, [my mother](people/person_1606.qmd) has become so much more feeble and seems to be losing her appetite, but it is most thank worthy that she is quite free from all suffering. 

Yours sincerely
<C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Edith Crawley was a second cousin of CMY's, and was one of the women who accompanied the Rt. Rev. [Robert Gray](people/person_578.qmd) and his wife Sophia (Myddleton) Gray (d.1871) on his return to his diocese of Cape Town. They included Mary Anderson Morshead, and [Anna Jane (Fair) Seymour](people/person_495.qmd); the latter may have been the older lady CMY mentions.
